methodology.evidence_policy: Only provider, agency, facility, foundation, or provider-linked application pages were accepted as evidence. Aggregators were not used. The all-opportunities view contains verified records from the documented searched-source universe, not unverified search noise or an internet-wide exhaustive list.
methodology.endpoint_rule: Endpoint liveness and program openness are checked separately. A live page or form can belong to an archived or repurposed call; a moved page can point to a valid new route. Application controls are suppressed for tracker-archived records even when an official endpoint remains live.

status_definitions.open: Official evidence showed current intake and the modeled cycle remained outside the tracker’s inclusive 15-calendar-day lead-time archive fence.
status_definitions.upcoming: Official evidence promised a future round outside the archive fence while intake or an application route was not yet available.
status_definitions.closed: Archived/non-actionable in this tracker because the sponsor closed intake, the modeled cycle passed, or a verified fixed applicant deadline was within 15 calendar days. A visible retirement reason distinguishes tracker policy from sponsor closure.
status_definitions.stale-endpoint: An application endpoint is dead or no longer serves the named call even though old official content may still link it. Program status and endpoint status are recorded separately whenever possible.

Official Tables 2/3 amended July 27, 2026 show D.6 Astrophysics Research and Analysis with a mandatory June 25, 2026 NOI and an August 6 proposal deadline. The official D.7 Strategic Astrophysics Technology page says notices of intent were requested by June 25 and proposals are due August 6; it does not call the notice mandatory. D.6 is non-actionable after its mandatory step, while D.7’s final deadline is inside the inclusive 15-day archive fence. Neither is promoted through this umbrella navigation card; each requires a distinct stable ID and element-level review. NASA’s solicitation, element page and due-date tables are the controlling sources.
